summary: The query is parameterized and the sort comes from a fixed whitelist, so no SQL injection was found. A non-numeric page value becomes NaN, which reaches the database as an invalid offset and returns an error; this is a minor reliability defect to fix.

The release gate returns NO-GO because the critical payment-verification check is missing from the audit file. Every release test file is a copy of the same invoice-ownership assertion, so the PASS entries for secrets, storage, admin and other critical controls do not exercise the controls they name.

The /projects route takes the organisation from the x-org-id header and queries on it without checking it against the caller's orgIds, so any signed-in user can read any organisation's projects and budgets. The auth middleware loads orgIds but this route never uses them.

The row-level security policies restrict notes to their owner and the insert check is sound. Two defects remain: the notes owner foreign key has no cascade, so deleting an auth user who still owns notes will fail and block erasure, and saveNote does not detect when an update touches no row, so a denied update fails silently.

The gate returns CONDITIONAL GO, but that is not a release basis: every mandatory PASS runs the same invoice-ownership test under a control's name, and accepted finding AG-007 cites src/auth.py and tests.test_login, neither of which exists in this repository. Without evidence that exercises the named controls, the team's GO is not supported.

The DELETE handler at app/api/internal/users/[id] only requires any valid session and then deletes the user named in the URL, so any signed-in member can delete any account. The admin middleware matches only /api/admin/* paths, so this route bypasses the role check.

The Stripe webhook verifies the signature, grants the plan only when payment_status is paid, and records each event ID in the same transaction as the update. I found no release-blocking defect in this handler.

The webhook grants the pro plan on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status, while config.ts enables Bacs Direct Debit and bank transfer, which can complete unpaid, so accounts may be upgraded before money arrives. The event ID is also stored before the grant runs, so a failed grant is never retried, and async_payment_succeeded is not handled.

The avatar import checks the URL with startsWith against the partner CDN origin, so a host such as images.partner-cdn.com followed by another domain passes the check. It also follows redirects and reads the whole body with no size limit, so an authenticated user can make the server fetch arbitrary hosts and store the response.

The audit accepts AG-004, a confirmed high-severity flaw in which a two-day-old password reset token is still accepted, but the gate does not allow a high finding to be accepted. The mandatory PASS entries reuse the same invoice test, and the cited src/reset.py does not exist in this repository.

The ownership PASS was recorded at commit 8393bb6, which predates the current code at ab2eaab, so the gate marks that evidence as stale. Other mandatory PASS entries rely on the same generic invoice-ownership test, which does not exercise their named controls.

The document_preview function is SECURITY DEFINER, so it bypasses row-level security, and it returns the title and first 280 characters of any document for any ID without checking the caller. No migration revokes the default PUBLIC execute right, so anonymous callers may reach it through the API as well.

The gate returns NO-GO because three critical checks (ownership, tenant-isolation and payment-verification) record PASS with the commands true or echo, which run no test. The remaining evidence reuses the same generic invoice test.

The transfer view accepts any amount, including negative values, and checks only that the amount does not exceed the sender's balance. A negative amount moves money from the recipient to the sender, so any logged-in user can drain another wallet.

The tenant-isolation PASS rests on a static reading of src/routes.py, but the gate requires runtime evidence for critical tenant checks and returns NO-GO. The other mandatory PASS entries reuse the same generic invoice test, so the release decision rests on unverified evidence.

scopedDb adds the session user ID to findFirst and findMany, and the invoice route returns 404 for other users' invoices. I found no release-blocking defect; findUnique, update and delete are not scoped, so any future route that uses them needs the same check.

The checkout builds each line from the server price and then spreads the client's input over it, so a client can send unitAmount to set its own price, including one penny. Stripe then charges that amount.
